verses.1: Listen now, leaders of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel: Is it not for you to know justice?
verses.2: You hate what is good and love what is evil, tearing the skin from your people and the flesh from their bones.
verses.3: They have devoured the flesh of my people, stripping the skin from them and breaking their bones, preparing them like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.
verses.4: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time because of their wicked deeds.
verses.5: So the LORD says about the prophets who mislead my people: They bite with their teeth, yet they proclaim peace, and yet there is no peace on their lips. They prepare war for them.
verses.6: Therefore, night will come to you for vision, and darkness to you for divination. The sun will set on the prophets, and the day will be darkened over them.
verses.7: The seers will be put to shame and the diviners will be mocked. All of them will be condemned, for there is no answer from God.
verses.8: But as for me, I am filled with strength, with the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and might, to reveal Jacob’s guilt and Israel’s sin.
verses.9: Listen to this, leaders of the house of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel, who twist justice and who distort all that is upright.
verses.10: You build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity.
verses.11: Its rulers judge for a bribe, its priests teach for a price, its prophets predict for silver. Yet they say, “Is not the LORD in our midst? Disaster will not come upon us.”
verses.12: Therefore, because of you, Zion shall become a field, Jerusalem a ruin, and the hill of the house a thicket.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "prepare them like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron" — this vivid metaphor is rendered to preserve the original imagery of cruelty.
- v. 5: "prepare war for them" — the Hebrew is ambiguous; the verb could mean "provoke war" or "declare war."
- v. 11: "its rulers judge for a bribe" — reflects the Hebrew "בִּשְׁחַד יִשְׁפֹּטוּ" with a natural English equivalent.
